To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the service provider can incentivize users to maximize their location privacy and, at the same time, increase the number of services that they receive, by providing a service level that depends on the privacy type of users.

(1) the service provider (the Company) can increase its revenue if it adopts a game-theoretic approach, (2) a privacy-aware User can increase her location privacy by adopting a game-theoretical approach, and (3) the Company can maximize its profit by adopting a non-strategic approach, but this is only possible when the User has a low level of privacy awareness.
the Company's strategy can outperform non-strategic approaches in terms of revenue, while the User's strategy can maximize his privacy and the service level he receives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how a company can incentivize a user to maximize his privacy, while the company can still maximize its profit.
the problem of how to incentivize users to consent to location tracking.
the problem of incentivizing a privacy-aware User to stay connected, so that the Company can collect his location information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed game-theoretic model of incentivizing privacy-aware users to stay connected is a novel and promising approach to the location privacy problem.
our approach is the best solution to maximize the User's privacy while maximizing the Company's profit, and it is better than the other methods.

, in the case of a User with high privacy awareness, the Company should not incentivize the User to stay online for long periods of time, but should offer him a high level of services, in order to maximize its profit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the User's privacy type is the key parameter that influences the User's decision to remain connected or not.

we have developed a model to analyze the trade-off among location privacy, service level, and profit of the company, and have shown that our game-theoretic approach outperforms the existing non-strategic methods.

we have proposed a game theoretic model to determine the service level that would maximize the profit of the Company and at the same time, incentivize the User to stay online for a long time, thus, maximizing his location privacy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Company can incentivize the User to stay online as long as possible, and still protect the User privacy.

the User is willing to trade-off his location privacy for a better service level, and this is a win-win situation for the Company, which increases its profit, and for the User, which experiences better services.

the Company can incentivize users to consent to tracking, by offering them a certain level of services that they would not otherwise experience, and that this level of services depends on the User's privacy type.
